title: KAFKA-21081: Skip key and value decoding on timestamp lookup paths
body:
`FileRecords.searchForTimestamp`, `RemoteLogManager.lookupTimestamp` and
`RecordBatch.offsetOfMaxTimestamp` iterate records only to read
`timestamp()` and `offset()`, but they use `streamingIterator`, which
for compressed batches allocates and copies every record's key, value
and headers. `skipKeyValueIterator` (KAFKA-8106) skips the body instead,
but it was only declared on `MutableRecordBatch`, so the file-backed
`FileChannelRecordBatch` could not use it.

The skip iterator never allocates a buffer sized by a record, so these
paths do not need `max.decompressed.message.bytes` either: an oversized
record cannot blow up a lookup, and a lookup no longer fails when the
limit is lowered below an already-stored record.

Changes:

- moves `skipKeyValueIterator` from `MutableRecordBatch` to
`RecordBatch`
and implements it on `FileChannelRecordBatch` by delegating to
`loadFullBatch()`;
- adds `PartialLegacyRecord`, so compressed v0/v1 batches skip the key
and value too instead of falling back to a full decode;
- removes `maxRecordBodySize` from `skipKeyValueIterator`,
`readPartiallyFrom` and the timestamp lookup paths. `streamingIterator`
keeps it;
- switches the three lookup paths to `skipKeyValueIterator`;
- updates the `max.decompressed.message.bytes` doc.

`LogValidator` uses `skipKeyValueIterator` on the in-place path, so it
no longer rejects an oversized compressed record there, and the produce
tests from https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23429 that expected it
are removed. The cleaner side is handled by KAFKA-21082 and KAFKA-21100.

Reviewers: Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>
